title: Mother of Pearl Meaning, Properties & Benefits
subtitle: The light a shell makes for itself.
lead: Mother of pearl meaning explained: what nacre is, how a shell builds it, the meaning of calm, purity and protection it carries, and how to wear and care for it.
paras: ## What is mother of pearl?

Mother of pearl, also called nacre, is the smooth, iridescent layer that lines the inside of certain shells. Pearl oysters and freshwater mussels make it to protect their soft bodies, and they make pearls from exactly the same material. It is organic: not a mineral dug from the ground, but something a living animal builds, layer by layer.
## How the shimmer forms

Nacre is made of tiny flat platelets of aragonite, a form of calcium carbonate, stacked like bricks and held together by a thin organic protein called conchiolin. Each platelet is about as thin as a wavelength of visible light. When light passes through the stacked layers it is reflected and bent at every level, which creates the soft, moving rainbow sheen called orient, or iridescence.
## Mother of pearl properties at a glance

Material: nacre, aragonite platelets bound by conchiolin.
Origin: the inner shell of pearl oysters and freshwater mussels.
Colour: creamy white, silver, pink and grey, with a rainbow sheen.
Hardness: about 3.5 on the Mohs scale.
Main sources: freshwater farms in China; pearl oysters from the South Seas, Australia, the Philippines and French Polynesia.
## Mother of pearl meaning

Born in the sea and built slowly, mother of pearl has long been linked with calm, purity and protection. In many coastal cultures it was carried as a charm for travellers on the water, and it is often associated with the moon and the tides. In modern crystal tradition it is worn as a reminder to stay gentle and steady. These are cultural beliefs rather than scientific properties: we share them because many people choose a material for what it represents.
## Mother of pearl and pearls

A pearl and mother of pearl are the same substance in two forms. Mother of pearl lines the shell; a pearl forms when the animal coats an irritant inside its body with layer after layer of that same nacre. That is why both share the same glow, and where the name comes from: the shell lining was seen as the mother of the pearl.
## Mother of pearl and abalone

Abalone shell, with its blue-green and violet flashes, is also a kind of nacre, from a different family of sea snails. Ours is the calmer, white-silver mother of pearl; abalone has its own page in our compendium.
## How to wear mother of pearl

Its light is quiet, so it pairs well with dark stones. In our new bracelet, 4 mm cubes of mother of pearl alternate with thin hematite discs: white and graphite, soft and metallic. It is slim enough to wear next to a watch or stacked with other bracelets.
## How to care for mother of pearl

Mother of pearl is soft and organic, so treat it gently. Put it on after perfume, lotions and hairspray; take it off before swimming, showering and the gym; and wipe it with a soft dry cloth. Keep it apart from harder stones so its surface does not scratch.
## Frequently asked questions

Is mother of pearl a real gemstone?
It is an organic gem, like pearl, amber and coral: made by a living organism rather than formed as a mineral.

Is mother of pearl the same as pearl?
It is the same material, nacre. Mother of pearl is the lining of the shell; a pearl is a separate bead of nacre.

Can mother of pearl get wet?
Occasional splashes are fine, but long contact with water, chlorine or soap can dull it over time.

Is mother of pearl natural?
Yes, ours is natural nacre cut from shell. Its colour and sheen vary from piece to piece.

lead: A guide to men's beaded bracelets in natural stone: which stones men choose, 10 mm or 12 mm beads, stone with sterling silver, and how to find your size.
paras: ## What makes a good men's beaded bracelet

A men's beaded bracelet works when it looks solid rather than decorative. That comes down to three things: natural stone with real weight, beads large enough to hold their own next to a watch, and a calm palette of black, grey, brown and deep blue. Every bracelet in this guide is strung by hand, stone by stone, in our atelier in Rome.
## 10 mm or 12 mm beads?

Bead size changes the character of a bracelet more than anything else.
8 mm: discreet, easy to stack, works on slim wrists.
10 mm: the everyday size for most men, visible without being loud.
12 mm: a statement bracelet with real presence, best on its own or with one thinner piece.
If you are unsure, start with 10 mm. Our size guide shows every size side by side on the wrist.
## The stones men choose most

Tiger's eye: golden-brown stripes that move in the light. Traditionally the stone of confidence, will and focus.
Blue tiger's eye: the same fibrous quartz in blue-grey, calmer and cooler. Linked with clarity and patience.
Black obsidian: volcanic glass, deep black and glossy, or matte when the surface is softened. Seen as a shield, a stone of truth.
Hematite: metallic grey and noticeably heavy. The Romans used it, and it is still worn for grounding and focus.
Lava stone: porous, matte and light, formed from cooled lava. A symbol of raw strength and stability.
Black onyx: ancient Romans carried onyx amulets into battle. Strength and grounded protection.
Picasso jasper: graphic black lines on cream, for creative, grounded focus.
Gibeon meteorite: real iron-nickel meteorite from Namibia, more than 4 billion years old. The rarest material we work with.
## Natural stone with sterling silver

Adding silver lifts a stone bracelet without making it flashy. We use handmade Bali beads in 925 sterling silver, crafted in Indonesia, set between the stones. A sterling silver tiger's eye bracelet is the classic choice: the warm gold of the stone against cool silver. Matte obsidian with silver is the most understated combination we make.
## Stacking and wearing with a watch

Wear a single 12 mm bracelet on the wrist without a watch, or a 10 mm bracelet next to the watch. To stack, combine one statement bracelet with one thinner one, and keep to two or three colours. Matte and polished stones together, such as matte hematite with polished tiger's eye, add depth without clutter.
## Handmade in Rome

Each bracelet is assembled by hand in our Roman atelier and finished with a scratch-resistant stainless steel bead carrying our logo. Natural stones vary, so the size and colour of the beads can differ slightly from the photos: no two bracelets are exactly alike.
## Ordering online

We are an online shop and, for now, ship from Italy to the European Union, Switzerland, Norway and the United Kingdom. Shipping is free on orders from € 50. Each piece is prepared in 3 to 5 working days, then delivered in 2 to 5 days. Returns are accepted within 30 days.
## Frequently asked questions

Are these bracelets only for men?
No. They are unisex: the larger beads and darker stones are simply the ones men tend to choose.

Which stone is best for a first bracelet?
Tiger's eye or black obsidian in 10 mm. Both go with everything.

Are the stones natural?
Yes, each stone is natural unless the product page says otherwise. Every stone has its own page in our compendium.

title: Bracciali uomo con pietre naturali, fatti a mano a Roma
subtitle: Occhio di tigre, ossidiana, ematite e lava, infilati a mano a Roma.
lead: Guida ai bracciali uomo in pietre naturali: le pietre più scelte, perle da 10 o 12 mm, pietre con argento 925 e come trovare la misura giusta.
paras: ## Che cosa rende bello un bracciale uomo

Un bracciale uomo funziona quando sembra solido, non decorativo. Contano tre cose: pietra naturale con un peso vero, perle abbastanza grandi da stare accanto a un orologio e una tavolozza sobria di nero, grigio, marrone e blu profondo. Ogni bracciale di questa guida è infilato a mano, pietra per pietra, nel nostro laboratorio a Roma.
## Perle da 10 o da 12 mm?

La misura delle perle cambia il carattere del bracciale più di ogni altra cosa.
8 mm: discreto, facile da abbinare, adatto ai polsi sottili.
10 mm: la misura di tutti i giorni per la maggior parte degli uomini, visibile senza essere vistosa.
12 mm: un bracciale importante, con presenza; sta meglio da solo o con un bracciale più sottile.
Se hai dubbi, parti dai 10 mm. La nostra guida taglie mostra tutte le misure a confronto sul polso.
## Le pietre più scelte dagli uomini

Occhio di tigre: striature oro-bruno che si muovono con la luce. Per tradizione la pietra della sicurezza, della volontà e della concentrazione.
Occhio di tigre blu: lo stesso quarzo fibroso in blu-grigio, più calmo. Associato a lucidità e pazienza.
Ossidiana nera: vetro vulcanico, nero profondo e lucido, oppure opaco quando la superficie è satinata. Considerata uno scudo, una pietra di verità.
Ematite: grigio metallico e sorprendentemente pesante. La usavano già i Romani; si porta per stabilità e concentrazione.
Pietra lavica: porosa, opaca e leggera, nata dalla lava raffreddata. Simbolo di forza e stabilità.
Onice nera: gli antichi Romani portavano amuleti di onice in battaglia. Forza e protezione.
Diaspro Picasso: linee nere grafiche su fondo crema, per una concentrazione creativa.
Meteorite Gibeon: vero meteorite ferro-nichel dalla Namibia, con più di 4 miliardi di anni. Il materiale più raro che lavoriamo.
## Pietre naturali con argento 925

L'argento valorizza un bracciale in pietra senza renderlo vistoso. Usiamo perle Bali in argento 925 fatte a mano in Indonesia, inserite tra le pietre. L'occhio di tigre con argento è la scelta classica: l'oro caldo della pietra contro l'argento freddo. L'ossidiana opaca con argento è la combinazione più sobria che realizziamo.
## Come abbinarli e portarli con l'orologio

Porta un 12 mm da solo sul polso senza orologio, oppure un 10 mm accanto all'orologio. Per abbinarne più di uno, unisci un bracciale importante a uno più sottile e resta su due o tre colori. Pietre opache e lucide insieme, come ematite opaca e occhio di tigre lucido, danno profondità senza confusione.
## Fatti a mano a Roma

Ogni bracciale è assemblato a mano nel nostro laboratorio romano e rifinito con una perla in acciaio inossidabile antigraffio con il nostro logo. Le pietre naturali variano: misura e colore delle perle possono differire leggermente dalle foto, e non esistono due bracciali identici.
## Ordinare online

Siamo un negozio online e, per ora, spediamo dall'Italia in Unione Europea, Svizzera, Norvegia e Regno Unito. La spedizione è gratuita per ordini da 50 €. Ogni pezzo viene preparato in 3-5 giorni lavorativi e consegnato in 2-5 giorni. Accettiamo resi entro 30 giorni.
## Domande frequenti

Sono bracciali solo da uomo?
No, sono unisex: le perle più grandi e le pietre scure sono semplicemente quelle che gli uomini scelgono più spesso.

Quale pietra scegliere per il primo bracciale?
Occhio di tigre oppure ossidiana nera da 10 mm: stanno bene con tutto.

Le pietre sono naturali?

title: Gemstone Bracelet Meanings: What Each Stone Means
subtitle: 30 stones grouped by intention: calm, confidence, love, protection and luck.
lead: Stone bracelet meanings explained: what amethyst, tiger's eye, rose quartz, obsidian and 26 other gemstones traditionally mean, and how to choose yours.
paras: ## What does a stone bracelet mean?

For thousands of years people have chosen stones for what they represent as much as for how they look. Romans carried onyx into battle, Egyptians wore lapis lazuli as a sign of royalty, and today many people pick a bracelet for a quality they want to keep close: calm, confidence, love or protection. This guide lists the meaning traditionally given to each stone we work with, grouped by intention, so you can find the right one quickly.

A note on honesty: these meanings come from history, folklore and modern crystal tradition. They are cultural beliefs, not scientific or medical properties. We share them because a stone with a meaning you care about becomes a bracelet you wear every day.
## Stones for calm and a quiet mind

Amethyst: clarity, calm and intuition. The purple quartz long linked with a clear head and restful sleep.
Howlite: patience and a quiet mind. White with grey veins, a stone for slowing down.
Larimar: tranquil Caribbean seas. A rare blue stone found only in the Dominican Republic, worn for serenity.
Blue lace agate: gentle, honest communication. Soft blue bands that calm and steady the voice.
Aquamarine: serene flow and steady nerves. The sea-blue beryl of sailors and travellers.
Blue tiger's eye: calm clarity and patience. The cool, blue-grey side of tiger's eye.
## Stones for confidence and energy

Tiger's eye: confidence, will and focus. Golden stripes that move in the light.
Sunstone: warmth, leadership and light. A feldspar that glitters from within.
Red carnelian: vitality, courage and drive. Warm orange-red agate.
Apatite: focus, drive and clear thought.
Lapis lazuli: truth, royalty and wisdom. The deep blue prized since ancient Egypt.
## Stones for love and the heart

Rose quartz: unconditional, gentle love. The best-known stone of the heart.
Strawberry quartz: joyful, warm-hearted love. Clear quartz with red inclusions.
Red garnet: passion and devotion. A deep red stone exchanged as a promise.
Moonstone: intuition and new beginnings. A feldspar with a soft, moving glow.
## Stones for protection and grounding

Black obsidian: a shield of truth. Volcanic glass, deep black.
Black onyx: strength and grounded protection. Carried by Roman soldiers as an amulet.
Hematite: grounding, focus and stability. Metallic grey and heavy in the hand.
Lava stone: raw strength and stability. Porous rock formed from cooled lava.
Turquoise: protection and ancient wisdom. One of the oldest protective stones in the world.
Malachite: protection and steady growth. Bold green bands of copper mineral.
## Stones for balance and luck

Green jade: harmony, luck and serenity. A stone of good fortune in many cultures.
Sodalite: logic balanced with intuition. Navy blue with white veins.
Labradorite: magic, mystery and transformation. Grey stone with flashes of blue and gold.
Amazonite: courage, truth and balance. Soft green-blue feldspar.
Chrysanthemum fossil coral: a rare bloom of good fortune.
## Rare stones with a story

Gibeon meteorite: forged among the stars. Iron-nickel from space, more than 4 billion years old.
Lemurian quartz: ancient memory and wisdom. Quartz crystals with distinctive horizontal ridges.
Phantom quartz: growth layered over time. Crystals with ghost-like earlier growth inside.
Tridacna: purity and serene white. A marine material with a calm, minimal look.
## How to choose your stone

Start with the intention: pick the group above that matches what you want the bracelet to remind you of. Then trust the colour you are drawn to; most people choose a stone they like looking at, and that is the one they keep wearing. Finally, choose the bead size: 6 or 8 mm for a fine bracelet, 10 mm for every day, 12 mm for a statement.
## Can you wear several stones together?

Yes. Mixed bracelets combine stones with complementary meanings, such as hematite for grounding with tiger's eye for confidence, or howlite with sodalite for a calm, clear mind. Two or three different bracelets on the same wrist work the same way.
## Frequently asked questions

Which stone bracelet is best for anxiety and calm?
In crystal tradition: amethyst, howlite, larimar and blue lace agate. They are worn as reminders to slow down, not as a treatment.

Which stone means love?
Rose quartz above all, followed by strawberry quartz and red garnet.

Which stone is for protection?
Black obsidian, black onyx, hematite and turquoise are the traditional protective stones.

Which stone brings luck?
Green jade is the best-known stone of good fortune.

Are your stones natural?
Yes, unless the product page says otherwise. A few materials we use, such as Murano glass, Swarovski crystal, blue sandstone and cloisonné, are man-made, and their pages say so.

title: Amethyst in Motion
subtitle: Violet quartz, turned in the hand.
lead: A closer look at our Amethyst 06mm Bracelet: natural violet quartz, strung by hand in Rome, filmed so you see every band of colour.
paras: ## What is amethyst?

Amethyst is the violet variety of quartz. Its colour comes from traces of iron in the crystal, activated by natural radiation in the surrounding rock over very long periods. Tones run from pale lilac to deep purple, often in bands next to milky white quartz, as you can see in the video.
## A name from ancient Greece

The name comes from the Greek amethystos, “not intoxicated”: the ancient Greeks believed the stone kept its wearer clear-headed. Amethyst is the birthstone of February and is traditionally associated with calm, clarity and intuition.
## Properties at a glance

Mineral: quartz (silicon dioxide).
Colour: lilac to deep violet, often banded with white.
Hardness: 7 on the Mohs scale.
Main sources: Brazil, Uruguay, Zambia and many other countries.
## The 6 mm bracelet

Our Amethyst 06mm Bracelet is strung by hand in our atelier in Rome with natural 6 mm beads and one scratch-free stainless steel logo bead. Every bead is natural, so tone and size vary slightly from one bracelet to the next.
## Care

At 7 on the Mohs scale amethyst is made for everyday wear. Long hours in strong direct sunlight can slowly fade its colour, so store it away from a sunny windowsill, and keep it away from perfume and creams.

title: Sunstone Meaning, Properties & Benefits
subtitle: The feldspar that holds the light inside it.
lead: Sunstone meaning explained: the warm, glittering feldspar linked to joy, vitality and confidence. What it is, where it comes from and how to wear it.
paras: ## What does sunstone mean?

Sunstone is the stone of warmth and light. In crystal traditions it stands for joy, vitality, confidence and leadership: a stone worn to bring a little sunshine into the day. Its name comes from its look — a warm orange to red-brown body that sparkles from within whenever it catches the light.
## What is sunstone?

Sunstone is a feldspar, the same mineral family as moonstone and labradorite. Most gem-quality sunstone is oligoclase or labradorite feldspar. Its glitter comes from tiny flat platelets trapped inside the crystal: hematite in most sunstone, native copper in sunstone from Oregon. When light reaches them they flash like sparks, an effect gemologists call aventurescence.
## Sunstone properties at a glance

Mineral family: feldspar.
Colour: colourless, pale yellow, orange, red and red-brown.
Effect: aventurescence, a metallic glitter from hematite or copper platelets.
Hardness: 6 to 6.5 on the Mohs scale.
Main sources: Oregon (USA), India, Norway and Tanzania.
## Sunstone meaning in crystal tradition

In modern crystal lore sunstone is linked to the sacral chakra and is said to encourage optimism, independence and self-confidence, and to lift the mood on grey days. These are cultural beliefs rather than scientific properties. We share them because many people choose a stone for what it represents, and sunstone's message is a simple one: warmth, energy and light.
## Is sunstone the Vikings' sunstone?

Not quite. Norse sagas mention a “sólarsteinn”, a sunstone used to find the sun on cloudy days. Researchers believe it was most likely Iceland spar, a clear calcite that polarises light, rather than the orange feldspar sold as sunstone today. The two share a name, not a mineral.
## Sunstone and moonstone

Sunstone and moonstone are both feldspars, and they are often worn together: one warm and glittering, the other cool and glowing. Our Moonstone & Sunstone bracelets set them side by side, as a balance of day and night.
## How to wear sunstone

Sunstone's warm tone works with silver and gold alike, and next to dark stones it glows even more. In our atelier in Rome we string it in bracelets of 6, 8 and 10 mm beads and in irregular natural shapes, and we pair it with matte hematite, whose grey makes the orange stand out. At 6 to 6.5 on the Mohs scale it is a good stone for everyday wear, as long as it is kept away from hard knocks.
## How to care for sunstone

Clean it with lukewarm water, a drop of mild soap and a soft cloth, then dry it well. Avoid ultrasonic and steam cleaners, perfume and household chemicals, and store it apart from harder stones that could scratch it. Our care guide covers every stone we use.

title: Sodalite Meaning, Properties & Benefits
subtitle: Blue, stripped of excess.
lead: Sodalite meaning explained: the deep blue stone of logic, calm and clear communication. Its properties, origins and how to wear sodalite jewellery.
paras: ## What does sodalite mean?

Sodalite is the stone of clear thinking. In crystal traditions it stands for logic balanced with intuition, for calm, and for honest communication: a stone for people who prefer clarity over gloss. Its deep navy blue, cut by white veins, has the look of ink or a night sky.
## What is sodalite?

Sodalite is a sodium-rich mineral of the feldspathoid group, and its name comes from that sodium content. It was first described in the early 1800s from specimens found in Greenland. The white veins and spots that run through it are usually calcite.
## Sodalite properties at a glance

Mineral group: feldspathoid.
Colour: royal to navy blue, often with white veins; sometimes grey or violet tones.
Appearance: opaque, with a vitreous to slightly greasy lustre when polished.
Hardness: 5.5 to 6 on the Mohs scale.
Main sources: Brazil, Canada, Namibia, Greenland, Russia and the USA.
## Sodalite meaning in crystal tradition

In modern crystal lore sodalite is linked to the throat and third-eye chakras. It is said to quiet a busy mind, support rational thinking and help people express themselves honestly. These are cultural beliefs rather than scientific properties; we share them because the meaning of a stone is often the reason it is chosen.
## Sodalite or lapis lazuli?

The two are often confused: both are deep blue and both can show white veins. Lapis lazuli is usually a more even, brighter blue with golden flecks of pyrite. Sodalite tends to be darker and more veined, pyrite in it is rare, and it is slightly harder.
## How to wear sodalite

Sodalite's navy blue works especially well with silver, black and white. In our atelier in Rome we string it in 10 and 12 mm bead bracelets and pair it with howlite, hematite and lava stone, where the contrast makes the blue look deeper. It has presence but still reads as calm, so it is easy to wear every day.
## How to care for sodalite

Sodalite is softer than quartz, so keep it away from hard knocks and store it apart from harder stones. Clean it with lukewarm water, a drop of mild soap and a soft cloth, and avoid ultrasonic cleaners, acids and household chemicals.

lead: Blue topaz meaning explained: the clear blue gem of calm, truth and focus. What it is, where its colour comes from and how to wear blue topaz jewellery.
paras: ## What does blue topaz mean?

Blue topaz is the stone of calm clarity. Topaz has long been associated with truth and focus, and its blue variety is linked with honest communication, composure and a clear mind. Its colour, from icy sky blue to deep steel blue, makes that meaning easy to read.
## What is blue topaz?

Topaz is an aluminium silicate mineral that contains fluorine. It forms in granite pegmatites and similar rocks. Pure topaz is colourless; blue, yellow, pink and other colours come from trace elements or tiny defects in the crystal.
## Where does the blue colour come from?

Natural blue topaz exists, but it is usually very pale. Almost all the vivid blue topaz on the market, known in the trade as Sky Blue, Swiss Blue and London Blue, is colourless topaz that has been irradiated and heated to create a stable blue. It is a long-established and accepted treatment, and a reputable seller should always disclose it.
## Blue topaz properties at a glance

Mineral: topaz.
Colour: pale sky blue to deep inky blue.
Hardness: 8 on the Mohs scale, harder than quartz.
Cleavage: perfect in one direction, so a sharp blow can split it.
Main sources: Brazil, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Russia, Nigeria and the USA.
## Blue topaz meaning in crystal tradition

Over the centuries topaz has gathered many legends, most of them about strength, protection and a calm mind. In modern crystal lore blue topaz is connected to the throat chakra and is said to support clear expression, calm confidence and emotional balance. These are cultural beliefs rather than scientific properties.
## Is blue topaz a birthstone?
Topaz is the traditional birthstone for November, and blue topaz is also widely given for December birthdays. Blue topaz is the gemstone for the fourth wedding anniversary as well.
## How to wear blue topaz

Faceted blue topaz catches the light like few stones in its range. In our atelier in Rome we set faceted blue topaz beads against black matte beads in a slim bracelet, where the contrast lets the blue shine. We also offer loose faceted blue topaz for those who want to design their own piece.
## How to care for blue topaz

Despite its hardness, topaz can split along its cleavage, so avoid hard knocks. Clean it with warm soapy water and a soft brush. Avoid ultrasonic and steam cleaners, sudden temperature changes and strong heat, which can affect the colour.
